title: Reconstitution, displacement and final concentration
blurb: Add the powder's displacement to the diluent, find the final concentration, then draw up the right volume.
question: A 500 mg vial is reconstituted with 4.6 mL of water for injections; the powder displaces 0.4 mL. A person is prescribed 300 mg. What volume should be drawn up?

teach.body: Formal rule: final volume = diluent added + displacement volume; final concentration = drug in the vial ÷ final volume. Plain English: when you add water to a powder, the powder itself adds a little volume, so the vial ends up holding more liquid than you put in. The displacement value comes from the product information and is always given in the question. This is a stretch item on Part A.

teach.caption: The final volume, not the diluent volume, goes at the end of the sum.

teach.h: Worked example: Amira on a children's ward
teach.body: Amira Khan, 2, is prescribed 300 mg of an antibiotic from a 500 mg vial reconstituted with 4.6 mL; displacement 0.4 mL. Final volume = 4.6 + 0.4 = 5 mL, so 500 mg is in 5 mL (100 mg/mL). Volume = 300 ÷ 500 × 5 = 3 mL. Sense-check: 300 mg is three fifths of the vial, and three fifths of 5 mL is 3 mL.

teach.caption: Manufacturers often choose diluent volumes that make a round final volume.

teach.h: 300 mg from a 500 mg vial: with and without displacement
teach.caption: Ignoring displacement under-doses: the person gets less than prescribed.

teach.text: Using the diluent volume instead of the final volume. 4.6 mL of water plus 0.4 mL displacement makes 5 mL. Dividing by 4.6 mL gives the wrong concentration and the wrong volume to draw up.

teach.body: Sometimes you need a set final volume. For 10 mL from a 1 g vial with 0.6 mL displacement, add 10 − 0.6 = 9.4 mL of diluent. Subtract the displacement; do not add it. Keep weights and doses in the same unit: a 1 g vial is 1000 mg.

items.label: displacement is always in the stem

items: Concentration = drug in the vial ÷ final volume.
Volume to give = want ÷ have × final volume.
Classic error: using the diluent volume and ignoring displacement.
Diluent for a set final volume = final volume − displacement.

summary: You can now reconstitute a powder on paper: add the displacement to the diluent, find the final concentration and calculate the volume to draw up. You can also work backwards to the diluent volume needed for a set final volume.

A.q: A vial contains 500 mg of powder. The instructions say to add 4.6 mL of water for injections and that the powder displaces 0.4 mL. A person is prescribed 300 mg. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This uses the 4.6 mL diluent and ignores the 0.4 mL displacement.
whyNot.2: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.

A.q: A vial contains 1 g of powder. The instructions say to add 9.2 mL of water for injections and that the powder displaces 0.8 mL. A person is prescribed 750 mg. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.
A.why: Final volume = 9.2 + 0.8 = 10 mL, holding 1000 mg. Volume = 750 ÷ 1000 × 10 = 7.5 mL.

whyNot.0: This uses the 9.2 mL diluent and ignores the displacement (6.9 mL).
whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.2: This forgets to multiply by the 10 mL final volume.

A.q: A 250 mg vial is reconstituted with 4.8 mL of water for injections. The powder displaces 0.2 mL. What is the final concentration in mg per mL?

whyNot.1: This divides by the 4.8 mL diluent and ignores displacement.
whyNot.2: This divides volume by mass, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This divides by 50 instead of the 5 mL final volume.

B.q: A 600 mg vial is reconstituted with 5.6 mL of water for injections. The powder displaces 0.4 mL. A person is prescribed 450 mg. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This uses the 5.6 mL diluent and ignores displacement.
whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.

B.q: A child weighing 9 kg is prescribed cefuroxime 30 mg/kg by intravenous injection. A 750 mg vial is reconstituted with 7.5 mL of water for injections; the powder displaces 0.5 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.
B.why: Dose = 30 × 9 = 270 mg. Final volume = 7.5 + 0.5 = 8 mL. Volume = 270 ÷ 750 × 8 = 2.88 mL.

whyNot.1: This uses the 7.5 mL diluent and ignores displacement (2.7 mL).
whyNot.2: This forgets to multiply by the 8 mL final volume.
whyNot.3: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.

B.q: A 1 g vial has a displacement value of 0.6 mL. You need a final volume of exactly 10 mL. What volume of diluent should be added? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This adds the displacement instead of subtracting it.
whyNot.1: This ignores displacement: the vial would end up holding 10.6 mL.

C.q: A baby weighing 4.2 kg is prescribed a medicine 50 mg/kg by intravenous injection. A 500 mg vial is reconstituted with 4.6 mL of water for injections; the powder displaces 0.4 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.
C.why: Dose = 50 × 4.2 = 210 mg. Final volume = 5 mL. Volume = 210 ÷ 500 × 5 = 2.1 mL.

whyNot.0: This uses the 4.6 mL diluent and ignores displacement (1.93 rounds to 1.9).
whyNot.2: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This forgets to multiply by the 5 mL final volume.

C.q: A 1 g vial is reconstituted with 9.5 mL of water for injections. The powder displaces 0.5 mL. How many mg of the drug are in 1.8 mL of the reconstituted solution? Please use the correct unit.
C.why: Final volume = 10 mL, so the concentration is 1000 ÷ 10 = 100 mg/mL. 1.8 mL × 100 mg/mL = 180 mg.

whyNot.0: This divides by the 9.5 mL diluent and ignores displacement.
whyNot.1: This takes 1 g as 100 mg, so the concentration comes out tenfold too low.
whyNot.3: This reads 1.8 mL as 18 mL, a tenfold error.

C.q: A 2 g vial is reconstituted with 8.4 mL of water for injections. The powder displaces 1.6 mL. A person is prescribed 1.3 g. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.1: This uses the 8.4 mL diluent and ignores displacement (5.46 rounds to 5.5).
whyNot.2: This forgets to multiply by the 10 mL final volume (0.65 rounds to 0.7).
whyNot.3: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.

reteach.title: Diluent plus powder
reteach.question: You add 3.6 mL of water to a vial whose powder displaces 0.4 mL. How much liquid is in the vial?

blocks.body: 3.6 + 0.4 = 4 mL in the vial. If the vial held 200 mg, the concentration is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 mg/mL, and that is the strength you use for want ÷ have.

blocks.text: Dividing by the 3.6 mL of water. The powder's 0.4 mL is part of the solution you draw up from.

explain.body: Final volume = diluent + displacement. 3.6 mL + 0.4 mL = 4 mL.

test.q: A vial is reconstituted with 3.6 mL of water for injections. The powder displaces 0.4 mL. What is the final volume in the vial? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This subtracts the displacement instead of adding it.

test.q: A 500 mg vial has been reconstituted to a final volume of 5 mL. What is the concentration in mg per mL?

whyNot.0: This divides volume by mass, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This divides by 50 instead of 5, a tenfold error.

explain.body: With 50 mg in each mL, 165 mg needs 165 ÷ 50 = 3.3 mL.

test.q: A reconstituted solution contains 50 mg in 1 mL. A person is prescribed 165 mg. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.2: This divides by 5 instead of 50, a tenfold error.
whyNot.3: This uses 100 mg/mL, not the 50 mg/mL in the stem (1.65 rounds to 1.7).

test.q: A 1 g vial is reconstituted with 4 mL of water for injections. The powder displaces 1 mL. A person is prescribed 500 mg. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This uses the 4 mL diluent and ignores displacement.
whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
